findings.reason: The protected solution is clear, concise, and interview-ready. It decomposes the answer into the root, a preferred-child left walk, one iterative left-to-right leaf traversal, and a mirrored right walk whose temporary values are reversed. The is_leaf helper and structural names expose the problem's essential distinctions without unnecessary machinery.

Leaves are excluded from both side walks and the root is excluded from leaf emission, so the three structural portions are disjoint. Falling back to the available child keeps each side walk on the outermost path, pushing right before left makes the stack visit leaves left-to-right, and reversing right_boundary produces the required bottom-to-top suffix. The singleton and missing-side cases are handled without duplication.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 545 and its Python boundaryOfBinaryTree(root) interface. The app-local TreeNode is the required explicit local equivalent of LeetCode's injected model, solve(root) accepts that structure, and the returned list preserves distinct nodes even when their integer values are equal.

The protected app source and immutable native source bound to verified submission 2065334731 have the same helper, loop order, child preferences, stack discipline, root exclusion, right-boundary reversal, and return data flow. Their only structural difference is the app-local TreeNode definition required by the standalone runner.

The three authored left-spine comb workloads span 63 through 1023 nodes and force every leaf plus both outer-boundary behaviors. The exact protected source passed all 10 refreshed correctness cases and all three performance tiers, including the legal 10,000-node deep-tree boundary. A correct control that explicitly copied every complete root-to-leaf path prefix matched every authored output but failed only the traced benchmark verdict with relative growth exponent +1.02 and a 77.99x largest runtime ratio.

The Approach exactly matches the current implementation: it derives the disjoint boundary roles, preferred-child side walks, right-first stack pushes for left-first visitation, and reversal of the collected right side. Its O(n) time and O(h) auxiliary-space bounds correctly account for the traversal stack and right-boundary list.

The modular Reference was reviewed directly in the authenticated Premium statement and bound to its rendered live-content hash. It preserves every boundary rule, both explained examples in order, both constraints, and the relationships from both source tree images through independently authored accessible Mermaid diagrams.

coverage: Both authenticated Premium source examples appear first and in source order with their exact level-order trees and anti-clockwise boundary results.
The invented single-node sample was relabelled as a trial, and the formerly hidden right-chain, fallback-child, and duplicate-value checks are now visible trials.
Contract boundaries cover one and 10,000 nodes, values -1000 and 1000, a 10,000-level legal chain, leaves at both extremes, balanced trees, skewed trees, and one-sided roots.

Material semantics cover left-child and right-child fallback, exclusion of boundary leaves from side lists, left-to-right leaf order, bottom-to-top right-boundary order, singleton nonduplication, and distinct nodes that carry equal values.

An independent recursive boundary-role oracle verified all ten correctness cases and all three benchmark outputs. The protected app and immutable native sources also agreed on 625 exhaustive shapes through seven nodes and 1,000 randomized trees.
All ten correctness cases are visible samples or trials; the unchanged 63-, 255-, and 1023-node comb workloads remain hidden and performance-only in benchmark.json.
